title: Plans per Loan and per Borrower — Payment Protection Provision
content:
**Provision.** Payment Protection is attached loan by loan: a borrower may hold Payment Protection plans on at most 2 loans at once (every personal loan they can hold), and no loan may carry more than one plan. For a new enrollment, the loan has no other Payment Protection plan in enrolled or active status, and a plan cancelled on this loan is never re-enrolled.

## How the provision is applied to an enrollment

The test is made before the enrollment is recorded, against the company's own plan records for **the same loan that is being enrolled** — the statuses of any Payment Protection plan already attached to that loan. Plans attached to the borrower's other loans do not decide the one-plan-per-loan test for this loan; they count only toward the limit of 2 loans with plans at once.

| Payment Protection plan already on the loan being enrolled | One-plan-per-loan condition |
|---|---|
| None | Met |
| A plan in enrolled status (still in its free-look period) | Not met |
| A plan in active status | Not met |
| A plan in cancelled status | Not met: a plan cancelled on this loan is never re-enrolled |

## Hypothetical cases

- *Two loans, one plan.* A borrower holds two personal loans; one already carries a Payment Protection plan in active status. Enrolling the other loan concerns a loan with no plan of its own, and brings the borrower to plans on 2 loans, which is within the limit.
- *Second plan on the same loan.* A loan already carries a plan in enrolled status. A further plan on that loan, of any type, would give the loan more than one plan, so the condition is not met.
- *Earlier cancellation.* A loan once carried a plan that the borrower cancelled. That loan is not re-enrolled, whichever plan is asked for.
